THIRD PARTY NOTICES
OpenPhantom patch
===============================================================================

This archive contains software from other people as well as ours. Their parts
stay under their own licences, and this file names them.

The full, unaltered licence text for the bundled components is in the file
dxwrapper-License.txt, next to this one. Please keep both files with the
archive: DxWrapper's licence requires its notice to travel with it.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. DxWrapper
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  Files      dxwrapper.dll
             ddraw.dll        (the DxWrapper stub loader)
             dxwrapper.ini    (configuration, not code)

  Version    1.8.8600.25
  Copyright  Copyright (C) 2025 Elisha Riedlinger
  Licence    zlib
  Source     https://github.com/elishacloud/dxwrapper

  DxWrapper is not part of OpenPhantom and is not covered by the MIT licence
  above. It is included because the game needs a DirectDraw translation layer
  on modern Windows, and this is the one the fixes were developed and tested
  against.

  The zlib licence permits redistribution, including in commercial products,
  subject to three conditions. In plain terms, as they apply here: we do not
  claim to have written DxWrapper, these binaries are unaltered originals, and
  the licence notice is included rather than stripped. The binding text is in
  dxwrapper-License.txt.

3. Components inside DxWrapper
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  dxwrapper.dll is not a single work. It carries code from other projects, each
  keeping its own licence. From DxWrapper's own licence notice:

    d3d8to9                   BSD 2-Clause
                              Copyright (C) 2015 Patrick Mours

    Detours, DirectXMath      MIT
                              Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation

    Hooking.Patterns          MIT
                              Copyright (c) 2014 Bas Timmer/NTAuthority et al.

    imgui                     MIT
                              Copyright (c) 2014-2025 Omar Cornut

    MemoryModule              Mozilla Public License 2.0
                              Copyright (c) 2004-2015 Joachim Bauch

  MemoryModule is the one with an obligation beyond attribution. The MPL is a
  file level copyleft: anyone receiving these binaries is entitled to the
  source of the MPL covered files. Nothing here is modified, so that duty is
  discharged by the upstream repository above, which carries the source of
  every component.

  Two further things were identified in the binary itself and are not named in
  DxWrapper's notice. They are recorded here for completeness rather than as a
  claim about their licensing:

    zlib compression library, deflate and inflate 1.1.4
      Copyright (C) 1995-2002 Jean-loup Gailly and Mark Adler

    Microsoft Direct3D 9 extensions (D3DX9) and the HLSL shader compiler
      Copyright (C) Microsoft Corporation


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. Not in this archive: what fmv_player uses
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  fmv_player.dll plays converted movies through libVLC, and tools\ converts
  them with FFmpeg. Neither is in this archive. They are named anyway, because
  a player who ends up with them on disk should be able to find out what they
  are and where they came from.

    libVLC (libvlc.dll, libvlccore.dll and its plugins)
      Licence    LGPL v2.1 or later
      Source     https://github.com/videolan/vlc
      Where      mods\fmv\, put there by the OpenPhantom installer, which
                 carries VideoLAN's own 32-bit build inside itself and copies
                 the unaltered files together with VideoLAN's own licence text
                 as mods\fmv\vlc-License.txt. Nothing is modified, so the
                 source duty is discharged by the repository above and by the
                 source archives on the release page.
                 fmv_player.dll loads it at run time and links against no part
                 of it at build time. A machine with this archive alone has no
                 libVLC and falls back to the game's original Bink playback.

    FFmpeg
      Licence    GPL v3 for the build the converter uses
      Source     https://ffmpeg.org/
      Where      mods\fmv\ffmpeg.exe when the OpenPhantom installer put it
                 there. With this archive alone, tools\convert_movies.ps1
                 downloads a pinned build into your own local application data
                 folder on demand and runs it from there. It is a tool the
                 player runs on files they already own, not a component of the
                 patch.

5. The game itself
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  No game data, executables, assets or other proprietary files are included in
  this archive or anywhere in the OpenPhantom project. You need your own
  legally obtained copy of Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace for PC.

  This is an independent fan project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or
  sponsored by LucasArts, Lucasfilm Ltd or Disney. All trademarks and related
